title: Novartis CEO Vasant Narasimhan on Transforming a 250-Year-Old Company

reader_summary.headline: We unlocked almost $180 billion of value.
reader_summary.overview: We unlocked almost $180 billion of value. Took this company that was a conglomerate and we turned it into four companies. We had these other businesses, but it was never really the core of who we are. Spinning off company sounds easy and retrospective.

thesis: Vasant Narasimhan argues that Novartis transformed from a conglomerate into a pure-play medicines company by spinning off three public companies to unlock nearly $180 billion in value. He explains that this strategic pivot was necessary because the company was previously misallocating capital, forcing it to sub-optimize its pharmaceutical business to support lower-return ventures like consumer health and generics.
